The rise of the Tang Dynasty likened Mount Hua to a dragon's horn and the Yellow River to its scales, with two eyes—one in Chang'an and the other at the Broken Gate.
This land's scenery resembles a painting, brimming with spiritual beauty. Geomancers called it the "Dragon's Eye," hence the saying: "Feast on the riches by the Wei River, rest in the blessed land of the Dragon's Eye."
After the Huang Chao Rebellion, the grand roads turned into thorny thickets, and the Xuanyuan Sect seized the chance to resurge here, only to be thwarted by the master of the Lone Cloud Gate.
Years later, as Chang'an fell, the Xuanyuan Sect claimed mastery over the nation's fate and possession of the Golden Peach, seeking to crown a righteous ruler and rise again from this very place.
